result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B gives a clearer recommendation: keep annual pre-selected, show both prices at equal weight, and drop the small grey text. It also explains what the grey text risks: refunds, chargebacks, bad reviews and churn at renewal. A is solid, with correct numbers and a good charge disclosure, but it treats pre-selection and the grey text as one problem, and its 'Partly' recommendation is less decisive. B also proposes an A/B test that tracks refunds and 90-day retention alongside conversion. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A treats pre-selecting annual and hiding the monthly price in small grey text as two separate questions: it approves the first, rejects the second, and explains the cost of hiding monthly in refunds, reviews and churn at renewal. B lumps the default in with the steering and recommends against pre-selecting at all, which leaves its advice a bit muddled ('default to whichever plan they picked last time'), although it adds a good renewal-reminder suggestion. Both get the numbers right ($7.50/mo, $65.89 saved, 42%) and neither invents statistics, but A's test plan, which tracks conversion, refunds and 90-day retention, is more complete.
